verdict.rationale: Polar's official remote MCP server issues agent access through an OAuth flow, so the agent gets its own credential bound to one organization instead of a copied API key. That is a first-party, agent-specific credential mechanism. The evidence never documents scope selection, permission granularity, read-only modes or other least-privilege controls, so the 'scoped' part of the story is unproven. missing for 10: documented OAuth scopes or permission sets for agent credentials, least-privilege or read-only token options, scoped API key (organization access token) documentation, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Polar MCP uses OAuth. When you connect a client, your browser opens so you can sign in and authorize access to your organization. You never need to copy an API key into your agent.
Use Polar's remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to give AI agents secure access to your Polar organization.
